Deal for diesel draws criticism

By A Reporter

The president announced a deal on Friday to buy diesel, a move critics said would fund the war rather than end it.

The first tranche is small relative to national consumption, according to traders who follow the market closely.

An investment strategist said the numbers mentioned were relatively small and unlikely to move prices for long.

He said the first tranche equated to about a day of demand, while longer contracts would take months to arrange.

Analysts expect the announcement to face legal challenges from several directions before any cargo is delivered.

The average diesel price is still well above last year's level.
